context.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
context.conclusion: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

record.type: real Euclidean vector space with measure
record.definition: V=R^n, realized as tuples (x_1,...,x_n). Its topology is the Euclidean topology and its measure dx is the product of n one-dimensional Lebesgue measures. Compactness, continuity and derivatives use these topologies; integrable means Lebesgue absolutely integrable.

W=R^m with inner product v·w=sum_{k=1}^m v_k w_k and norm |v|=(sum_{k=1}^m v_k^2)^(1/2). On V the same convention uses n coordinates. The squared norm and dot product in all formulas have this meaning.

u_t(x,r) is the derivative at r of the one-variable map ρ↦u(x,ρ). Derivatives are ordinary Fréchet derivatives in coordinate directions; outside their differentiability set use the total derivative convention zero. This convention grants no differentiability.

record.definition: u_jt(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r). Commutation with ∂_r u_j is a claim to be proved, not part of this definition.

e_t(x,r)=∂_r e(x,r), with the total derivative convention of D003.

record.statement: Let X be a measurable space, μ a measure on X, Z a normed additive commutative group and normed real vector space, I an index type and l a countably generated filter on I. Suppose eventually along l the functions Φ(i,·) are almost everywhere strongly measurable; eventually along l, |Φ(i,z)|≤β(z) for μ-almost every z; β is μ-integrable; and for μ-almost every z, Φ(i,z) tends along l to φ(z). record.statement: For every x∈V and r>0, u(x,r)·u_t(x,r)=0 and u_t(x,r)·(u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r))=0. Moreover u(x,r)·u_tt(x,r)=−|u_t(x,r)|^2, and for every 1≤j≤n, u(x,r)·u_jj(x,r)=−|u_j(x,r)|^2. For every real a satisfying u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r), a=sum_{j=1}^n|u_j(x,r)|^2−|u_t(x,r)|^2; consequently u_tt−Δu=(sum_j|u_j|^2−|u_t|^2)u pointwise. No derivative of a is asserted or used.

record.statement: For every t0>0 there exist a compact C⊂V and R>0 such that, with J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and Q=[−R,R]^n, C⊂(−R,R)^n, u(x,r)=q for x∉C and r∈J, and every positive-order coordinate partial derivative of u is zero on (V\C)×int J. For each r∈int J the sections of e,e_t,A,B_j,T_j,g_j and ∂_{x_j}g_j (1≤j≤n) are continuous, vanish outside C, have compact support, and are Lebesgue integrable on V. Each is bounded in absolute value on Q and its absolute integral is at most its bound times |Q|. The box Q is compact, measurable, has Lebesgue measure (2R)^n<∞, and C⊂int Q, so all these sections vanish on a neighborhood of ∂Q. In particular e(·,r) is integrable for every r>0.

record.statement: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

For measurable spaces X,Y with measures μ,ν, a normed additive commutative group Z with a normed real vector-space structure, and map χ:X→Y, if χ preserves μ and ν (it is measurable and its pushforward of μ equals ν) and χ is a measurable embedding, then for every φ:Y→Z, ∫_X φ(χ(z)) dμ(z)=∫_Y φ(w) dν(w). No integrability hypothesis is required for this total Bochner integral identity.
